title: SQL compilation artifact (fixture expected/ shape)
description: Deliberately lightweight: this catches gross authoring mistakes in a hand-written expected artifact (no SQL compiler exists yet to check these semantically, per #1630's context.md). It does not validate the SQL text itself, only the artifact's outer shape (AR-4: parameterized SQL text + ordered/named parameter list).

dialect.description: Which of the four v1 SQL dialects this artifact targets (§5) — Oracle is community-tested/OQ-6-open and excluded from this fixture suite for now.

sql.description: The parameterized SQL text. Must never contain a literal user value inlined as text (SEC-2) — only identifiers/keywords and parameter placeholders.

params.description: Ordered parameter values, one per placeholder in 'sql', in the placeholder's positional/named order. Each entry is the literal driver-bound value, not a tagged typedValue — by this stage the value has left the IR and become a query parameter. Usually a JSON string/number/boolean/null, but ALSO legitimately an array: SQL-4 (spec/semantics.md) binds a Postgres set membership as ONE array parameter ('"status" = ANY($1)' with params [["active","pending"]]), where dialects rendering 'IN (...)' bind N scalars instead. A decimal is a numeric STRING, never a JSON number (AR-7) — it and a double are otherwise the same wire shape. 'items: {}' is therefore deliberate: no per-entry validation here, because only the field's declared type distinguishes the legal shapes.
